author: RichardMCNgo

You can only trust someone’s conclusion to the extent that, if they’d seen the opposite findings, they would have shared the opposite conclusion.

Many papers studying misalignment don’t meet this bar.

I’m worried that a lot of work on AI safety evals is primarily motivated by “Something must be done. This is something. Therefore this must be done.”

I agree AI risk forecasts are basically guesses, and I dislike attempts to make them sound objective (eg many OpenPhil reports).

- @patrickc 

Full episode out tomorrow https://t.co/HuIGvZBWRQ

author: RichardMCNgo
text:
So apparently UK courts can decide that two unrelated jobs are “of equal value”.

And people in the “underpaid” job get to sue for years of lost wages.

And this has driven their 2nd biggest city bankrupt.

Am I getting something wrong or is this as crazy as it sounds?

author: RichardMCNgo
text: Today, physical survival is much easier than it used to be. But in many ways *psychological* survival has become harder. We construct our identities as individuals, rather than as members of predefined groups; and keeping those identities stable all by ourselves is hard work!

author: RichardMCNgo
text:
There’s a striking similarity between physicists hearing about nuclear chain reactions and AI researchers hearing about recursive self-improvement.

Key bottlenecks in both cases include willingness to take high-level arguments seriously, act under uncertainty, or sound foolish. https://t.co/w3bxXo3JbL

author: RichardMCNgo
text: Every word gets more surprising - anyone know what they’re talking about? https://t.co/3xM9QodXW3

author: RichardMCNgo
text: Even as AI makes physical goods and intellectual labor abundant, human attention and respect will remain scarce. It’s hard to buy those with money, so I expect that social media followers will become an increasingly important “currency”.

author: RichardMCNgo
text:
Epistemic status: mostly joking. But I do think kids’ neuroplasticity is way underrated, and that even an hour a day in VR could give them an intuitive grasp of very alien environments (e.g. nanoscale physics) comparable to our intuitive grasp of everyday physics.

See also:

quoted.text: You know how the visual cortex of blind infants rewires itself to process sound or touch? What if you hooked up their optic nerves to the internet instead? Imagine reading a page of text in a second, as easily as others recognise objects visually. The first true digital native.

author: RichardMCNgo
text: It’s not that I think the risks are that high, objectively speaking. But wouldn’t it be unbearably embarrassing to have your name go down in history as one of the people who died totally avoidable deaths only a few years before immortality became possible?

author: RichardMCNgo
text: The closer we get to the singularity the lower my risk tolerance gets. I’d already ruled out skydiving and paragliding. Last year I started wearing a helmet consistently while cycling. I think 2024 might be the year I give up skiing.

author: RichardMCNgo
text: As the essentials of life get far cheaper, I can imagine corporations competing to give them away. “A million people eat our free meals daily” will be a selling point for a totally unrelated product. Or maybe ads on the food will pay for what would count as gourmet meals today.

author: RichardMCNgo
text:
Catchy quote, but Bernard Arnault just became the richest man on earth; are you sure you want to short fashion?

Like it or not, when people gain material abundance, they mostly spend it on status. The real question is whether we can design status games that are positive-sum.

author: RichardMCNgo
RichardMCNgo
text:
Honorable mentions which aren’t really proverbs:
- I could care less
- “Those who would give up essential liberty to purchase a little temporary safety deserve neither”: the example that inspired this thread. Turns out it’s actually pro-taxation: https://t.co/I4hSgLiQh5

author: RichardMCNgo
text:
There’s weirdly strong selection for proverbs to evolve towards the exact opposite of their original meaning:
- Blood is thicker than water
- Exception that proves the rule
- A rolling stone gathers no moss
- Carpe diem 
- The road less traveled
- Great minds think alike

Others?

author: RichardMCNgo
text: Mixed feelings about this one. The dancing is exceptional. But IMO the quality of execution actually highlights the flaws of the medium. Solo dance performances like this feel… solipsistic? Atomized? Unnatural? My gut says this isn’t what dance is for. https://t.co/pU1xvoPF8Q

author: RichardMCNgo
text: All the discussion I’ve seen of AI partners assumes they’ll substitute for human partners. But technology often creates new types of abundance. So I expect people will often have both AI and human romantic partners, with the AI partner carefully designed to minimize jealousy.
